blocks.content: The Magistrate is not bound by the opinion formed by the investigating officer in the police report submitted under Section 173.

rows: Submitted when sufficient evidence exists to prosecute the accused person.
Submitted when evidence is insufficient or no prima facie case is made out.
Magistrate takes cognizance under Section 190 and issues process to the accused.
Magistrate may accept, reject and order further investigation, or treat it as a private complaint.

items: Section 207 CrPC strictly mandates providing free copies of the police report and connected documents to the accused without delay before commencement of trial.
Under Section 173(8) CrPC, submission of a final report does not preclude the police from conducting further investigation or submitting supplementary chargesheets.
The Magistrate takes cognizance of the offence under Section 190(1)(b) CrPC, not merely of the offender.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Upon completion of an investigation, the officer-in-charge of a police station must forward a final report to the Magistrate empowered to take cognizance under Section 173(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
The Magistrate is not bound by the conclusions of the investigating officer and may accept the report, order further investigation, or issue process against the accused.
Under Section 207 CrPC, the Magistrate must furnish the accused with a copy of the police report, FIR, statements recorded under Section 161, and relevant documents free of cost.
Even after submitting a final report, the police retain the statutory power to conduct further investigation and submit a supplementary report under Section 173(8) CrPC.
